newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castorseed eases on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Indian castorseed eases on profit-taking.

text.p: Indian castorseed September delivery prices on Monday eased marginally by 6/7 rupees to 1,147/1,148 rupees per quintal on fresh speculative selling at higher levels, dealers said.
"Improved arrivals at producing centres prompted profit-taking by the bull operators," one dealer said.
Arrivals of castorseed in the Gujarat region rose to 11,000/12,000 bags (75 kg each) against the daily average of 4,000/5,000 bags last week.
Groundnut oil fell by 2/3 rupees at 370 rupees per 10 kg on higher arrivals from southern India while inflows from Gujarat region (western India) remained at a low ebb.
In Rajkot spot groundnut oil moved up to 600 rupees per 15 kg from 580/585 rupees on shortage of ready stock.
Daily arrivals of groundnut seeds in the Gujarat region have fallen to 15,000/20,000 bags against daily average of 40,000/50,000 bags achieved last month.
In Bombay imported palm oil rose by 2/3 rupees at 262/263 rupees per 10 kg on the back of recovery in the world market.
"The price rise for imported palm oil may prove shortlived in the local market looking at the fresh arrivals of 5,000/5,500 tonnes at the Bombay port," one miller said.
